text: ENIGMA Carbon Census is the named study of 83 enrichment compounds.
quote: # Report: ENIGMA Carbon Census — A Tiered Knowledge Census of 83 Enrichment Compounds
heading: Report: ENIGMA Carbon Census — A Tiered Knowledge Census of 83 Enrichment Compounds

text: Of 83 compounds, all 83 resolved to structures, 54 linked to KEGG, and 9 met the stated callable criteria; lauric acid qualified through measured fitness rather than an ENIGMA-isolate call.
quote: Of 83 compounds (59 SSO-groundwater + 24 necromass), all 83 resolved to structures (InChIKey via PubChem), 54 linked to KEGG, but only **9 are "callable"** (review I1: callable = an ENIGMA-isolate utilizer call **or** a Tier-1 measured RB-TnSeq carbon-source fitness experiment). Eight are callable on an `enigma_isolate_call` basis (≥1 ENIGMA-isolate prediction with a catabolic, compound-degrading reaction in a genome); a ninth — **lauric acid** — is callable on a `measured_fitness` basis: it has a Tier-1 measured carbon-source growth experiment in the Fitness Browser, confirmed structurally by an InChIKey re-match (NB02c).

text: The dark set is concentrated in alkaloids, shikimates/phenylpropanoids, terpenoids, and fatty acids.
quote: By class, the dark set is dominated by exactly the predicted classes: Alkaloids, Shikimates/Phenylpropanoids, Terpenoids, and Fatty acids.

text: Reported dark fractions were 53/59 = 90% for groundwater and 21/24 = 88% for necromass.
quote: The dark fraction is nearly identical across sources (groundwater 53/59 = 90%, necromass 21/24 = 88%), so darkness is a chemical-class property, not a sampling-source artifact.
heading: 1. The census is mostly dark: 74 of 83 compounds have no isolate-level utilizer call

text: The nine nominally callable compounds are listed by chemical class; lauric acid qualifies only through measured fitness, and Abscisic acid has a two-strain call.
quote: The 9 callable compounds are overwhelmingly **pollutant-adjacent aromatics**: salicylic acid, 3-hydroxybenzoic acid, 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde, phthalic acid, terephthalic acid (all Shikimates/Phenylpropanoids), plus Phenylethylamine and xanthine (Alkaloids), Abscisic acid (Terpenoid, a single 2-strain call), and lauric acid (Fatty acid, on a measured_fitness basis only — review I1).
heading: 2. H1 (coverage gradient by chemical class) — not formally supported (underpowered); directional only

text: Xanthine's R02107 reaction reflects purine nitrogen acquisition, not carbon catabolism; the effective carbon-callable count is 8 rather than 9.
quote: One caveat on this set: **xanthine is mis-scored as carbon-catabolic** — its allowlisted reaction R02107 (xanthine→urate, xanthine oxidase) is the purine pathway, which is **nitrogen acquisition, not carbon catabolism**, so the carbon-callable set is effectively **8, not 9** (see Limitations).
heading: 2. H1 (coverage gradient by chemical class) — not formally supported (underpowered); directional only

text: The pre-registered uniform-class-coverage null was not rejected: χ²=5.07, p=0.53, df=6, using eight ENIGMA-isolate-callable compounds.
quote: But the **pre-registered null (uniform coverage across classes) is not rejected**: a χ² test on the 8 `enigma_isolate_call` callables by class (Shikimates 5/25, Alkaloids 2/26, Terpenoids 1/17, Fatty acids 0/10, Polyketides 0/2, AA/Peptides 0/2, mixed 0/1) gives **χ²=5.07, p=0.53 (df=6)**; adding the single measured-fitness lauric acid (Fatty acids 1/10) does not change the verdict.
heading: 2. H1 (coverage gradient by chemical class) — not formally supported (underpowered); directional only

text: The class-gradient analysis is underpowered and confounded by uneven annotation coverage.
quote: With only ~9 callables across 83 compounds the design is underpowered to detect a class gradient, and the directional pattern is further **confounded with annotation coverage** (which classes KEGG/ModelSEED/genome_depot annotate) rather than a clean biological degradability gradient.
heading: 2. H1 (coverage gradient by chemical class) — not formally supported (underpowered); directional only

text: Among genomes with at least one of eight isolate-call capacities, capacity breadth had mean ~1.19, median 1, and maximum 4.
quote: Among the 8 `enigma_isolate_call` capacities across genomes carrying ≥1 capacity, catabolic versatility is right-skewed (mean ~1.19, median 1, max 4 capacities per genome).
heading: 3. H2 (cross-module modularity) — not supported beyond a shared aromatic funnel

text: Because rare capacities compress the φ coefficient, the reanalysis used Haldane-corrected odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals and Jaccard indices from saved 2×2 counts.
quote: NB05 first reported co-occurrence with the **φ coefficient**, but φ compresses toward zero when a capacity is rare (most are present in tens-to-hundreds of 3109 genomes), which can hide a real multiplicative enrichment. Review I4 (NB05b) recomputes two interpretable effect sizes per pair from the saved 2×2 counts — a **Haldane-corrected odds ratio + 95% CI** and the **Jaccard index** — with no Spark re-run.
heading: 3. H2 (cross-module modularity) — not supported beyond a shared aromatic funnel

text: Cross-block pairs had median odds ratio 2.28, 4/15 confidence intervals entirely above 1, and median Jaccard approximately zero; within-other estimates were sensitive to near-zero counts.
quote: By pair class: within-aromatic median OR 1.12 (3/10 pairs with CI entirely > 1, median Jaccard 0.026); within-other median OR 7.43 (1/3, but driven by Haldane correction on near-zero counts); and the genuine modularity test — **cross-block** pairs (distinct lower pathways) — median OR 2.28 with 4/15 CI > 1 but **median Jaccard ≈ 0**.
heading: 3. H2 (cross-module modularity) — not supported beyond a shared aromatic funnel

text: Phenylethylamine co-occurred with 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde (OR 2.84, 95% CI 1.49–5.40, q=0.035, n11=11) and phthalic acid (OR 3.37, 95% CI 1.46–7.75, q=0.071, n11=6).
quote: The one biologically real cross-block signal the OR surfaces (and φ hid) is **phenylethylamine co-occurring with aromatic-funnel acids**: 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde + phenylethylamine OR 2.84 (95% CI 1.49–5.40, q=0.035, n11=11); phthalic acid + phenylethylamine OR 3.37 (95% CI 1.46–7.75, q=0.071, n11=6).
heading: 3. H2 (cross-module modularity) — not supported beyond a shared aromatic funnel

text: The report interprets phenylethylamine co-occurrence as aromatic-pathway overlap, citing conversion to phenylacetate and the paa/phenylacetyl-CoA route.
quote: This is **expected and mechanistically coherent**, because phenylethylamine is itself an aromatic-derived substrate (deaminated to phenylacetate, then the *paa*/phenylacetyl-CoA route), so versatile aromatic degraders tend to carry both.
heading: 3. H2 (cross-module modularity) — not supported beyond a shared aromatic funnel

text: Even enriched pairs had Jaccard ≈ 0.04; only 25 of 3109 genomes (0.8%) carried both aromatic and non-aromatic capacities.
quote: Crucially the **Jaccard stays ≈ 0.04** even for these enriched pairs — only ~4% of genomes with either capacity carry both — and only **25 of 3109 genomes (0.8%)** carry both an aromatic and a non-aromatic capacity.
heading: 3. H2 (cross-module modularity) — not supported beyond a shared aromatic funnel

text: Broad cross-module modularity was not supported; the positive co-occurrence signal falls within aromatic-derived catabolism.
quote: **Verdict: no broad cross-module modularity**; the one positive signal is itself aromatic-derived, i.e. co-occurrence *within* the broad aromatic-catabolism phenotype, not modular co-assembly of mechanistically-distinct modules.
heading: 3. H2 (cross-module modularity) — not supported beyond a shared aromatic funnel

text: Utilizer counts and high-versatility genera are concentrated in Burkholderiales.
quote: What *is* supported is phylogenetic concentration — Burkholderiales dominate utilizer counts, and high-versatility genera (Polaromonas, Alcaligenes, Burkholderia, Paraburkholderia, Comamonas, Hydrogenophaga) cluster in that order.

text: With n=9 callable compounds, physicochemical comparisons were directional and used uncorrected p values; the quote preserves the reported medians and p values.
quote: NB09 Part 1 resolves PubChem physicochemical descriptors for all 83 compounds and contrasts callable vs dark. **With only n=9 callable this is directional, not inferential** (Mann–Whitney, reported as direction + uncorrected p). Callable compounds are consistently **smaller and structurally simpler** than dark ones: median Complexity 133 vs 207 (p=0.034), MolecularWeight 152 vs 179 (p=0.066), HeavyAtomCount 11 vs 13 (p=0.057), with directionally higher polarity (TPSA 57 vs 41, H-bond donors 2 vs 1).
heading: 7. Bioavailability/physicochemistry is a ceiling on the atlas: callable compounds are smaller and simpler (directional, underpowered)

text: Callable-versus-dark physicochemical differences may reflect annotation coverage as much as biological bioavailability.
quote: The honest reading is that this is at least as much an **annotation-coverage ceiling** as a biological-bioavailability one — simple, common, pollutant-adjacent aromatics are exactly the molecules KEGG/ModelSEED/genome_depot annotate, so "callable" tracks structural simplicity partly because the knowledge base does.
heading: 7. Bioavailability/physicochemistry is a ceiling on the atlas: callable compounds are smaller and simpler (directional, underpowered)

quote: The ENIGMA Carbon Census is **~89% organism-dark** (74/83 compounds with no isolate utilizer call) — the actionable product of a knowledge census can be the map of ignorance, and that map is biased exactly by chemical class (alkaloids/terpenoids dark, aromatics callable), not by sampling source (groundwater 90% vs necromass 88% dark).
heading: Discoveries

text: In the queried genomes, callable capacity concentrates in Burkholderiales, with 675 single-capacity genomes versus 18 carrying ≥3 capacities.
quote: Callable catabolic capacity among these compounds is **phylogenetically concentrated in Burkholderiales** and is a **specialist** trait: 675 single-capacity genomes vs only 18 generalists (≥3 capacities).
heading: Discoveries

text: Only 25/3109 genomes carry both aromatic and non-aromatic capacities (Jaccard ≈ 0); a phenylethylamine×aromatic association has Haldane OR ≈ 2.8–3.4.
quote: Cross-module co-occurrence is near-zero in share terms (Jaccard ≈ 0; only 25/3109 genomes carry both an aromatic and a non-aromatic capacity), even though a Haldane odds ratio surfaces a modest phenylethylamine×aromatic enrichment (OR ≈ 2.8–3.4) that is itself aromatic-derived — so versatility is a clade trait, not a portable module set.
heading: Discoveries

text: The n=9 callable comparison found median Complexity 133 versus 207 for dark compounds (uncorrected Mann–Whitney p=0.034). This is directional only and partly reflects an annotation-coverage ceiling: curated catabolism resources preferentially cover simple, pollutant-adjacent aromatics.
quote: **Directional only (n=9 callable, uncorrected p):** "callable" tracks **structural simplicity** — callable compounds have median Complexity 133 vs 207 for dark (Mann–Whitney p=0.034, uncorrected) — and this is at least partly an annotation-coverage ceiling, since simple pollutant-adjacent aromatics are the molecules curated catabolism resources cover.
heading: Discoveries

text: Six named dark compounds have biosynthetic associations but no catabolic link in this census, distinct from the 29 compounds without KEGG links.
quote: The dark set is **not uniformly orphan**: 6 dark compounds (Tyramine, guanidineacetic acid, cinnamic acid, caffeic acid, palmitic acid, farnesol) are biosynthesis-known/catabolism-unknown — MIBiG-consult triage targets distinct from the 29 fully-orphan (no-KEGG) compounds.

text: The report's literature context describes terephthalate conversion through terephthalate dioxygenase to protocatechuate in Pseudomonadota, including Ideonella and Comamonas, and actinobacterial degraders.

heading: Literature Context

text: Soil–freshwater significance values are uncalibrated because non-independent metagenomes and compositional, zero-inflated abundances yield all 83 genera at q<0.05, many near q~1e-70.
quote: Each metagenome is treated as an independent observation in a rank test over compositional, zero-inflated relative abundances; with thousands of non-independent samples this inflates significance massively (all 83 genera reach q<0.05, many at q~1e-70).
heading: Limitations

text: The report treats contrast direction and rank as useful but rejects its p-values as calibrated significance; it favors the label-free outlier mode.
quote: The *direction and rank* of the contrast are trustworthy and biologically sensible; the *p-values are not* and should not be quoted as calibrated significance. The label-free outlier mode (Arm B) is the more defensible discovery signal.
heading: Limitations

text: The global atlas is an abundance-based biome-occupancy proxy, not an activity measurement.
quote: **Abundance ≠ activity.** No environmental dataset measures the census compounds; the entire global atlas is a biome-occupancy proxy.
heading: Limitations

text: H3 is untestable here because its n=2 necromass callables are fully confounded with phthalate chemistry.
quote: **H3 is genuinely untestable** with these compounds (n=2 necromass callables, fully confounded with phthalate chemistry) — reported as such rather than forced.
heading: Limitations

text: The 8 isolate calls depend on a genome-prevalence-<10% compound-direction filter using KEGG degradation maps or a 3-reaction curated allowlist.
quote: The 8 `enigma_isolate_call` callables rest on a genome-prevalence-<10% signature-reaction filter that keeps a reaction only if it is catabolic *for the compound* (KEGG degradation map membership or a 3-reaction curated allowlist).
heading: Limitations

text: The callable/dark fraction is filter-dependent; the 9th callable, lauric acid, comes from independent measured-fitness evidence.
quote: A different filter would move the callable/dark boundary; the dark fraction is conditional on this choice. The 9th callable (lauric acid) is on an independent `measured_fitness` basis and is not subject to this filter.
heading: Limitations

text: The physicochemical comparison has only n=9 callable compounds and uncorrected Mann–Whitney p-values, so it is descriptive rather than calibrated inference.
quote: With only n=9 callable, the NB09 Part 1 contrasts (callable compounds smaller/simpler) are **directional only**, reported with uncorrected Mann–Whitney p-values; they should be read as descriptive, not as calibrated significance.
heading: Limitations

text: A bacterial purine carbon-utilization route exists through a distinct anaerobic gene cluster that this project did not score. The R02107 category error must not be generalized to all purine carbon catabolism.
quote: A bacterial *carbon* route for purines exists but is a distinct anaerobic gene cluster this project does not score.
heading: Limitations

text: The carbon allowlist no longer contains R02107, but the committed tables still contain xanthine pending regeneration.
quote: R02107 has now been removed from the carbon allowlist in `build_nb03.py`; the committed deliverable tables still include xanthine because they were not regenerated after the fix, but a re-run of NB03→NB04→NB08 would drop it.
heading: Limitations

text: Zero literature rescues from a PubMed-title-only screen do not establish that catabolic evidence is absent; the report cites class-level literature for monoterpenes and nicotine.
quote: Class-level catabolic literature exists for monoterpenes (Marmulla & Harder, *Front. Microbiol.* 2014) and alkaloids such as nicotine (Huang et al., *Front. Microbiol.* 2020); NB02b's zero literature-rescues reflect a PubMed-title-only screen, not absence of evidence.
heading: Limitations

text: Signature-completeness labels are not comparable across compounds: terephthalic acid requires 1 reaction and trivially reaches 1.0, unlike phthalic acid's 3-reaction signature.
quote: **"High-certainty" is not comparable across compounds.** `sig_completeness` is the fraction of each compound's *own* signature reactions a genome carries, so a single-reaction signature (terephthalic acid, 1 required reaction) trivially scores 1.0 ("high") for any carrier, while a 3-reaction signature (phthalic acid) cannot.
heading: Limitations

text: The reported 34/34 high-certainty terephthalic calls are a weak single-reaction-signature result, not especially strong evidence.
quote: The "terephthalic 34/34 high" headline is therefore the *weakest* completeness call, not the strongest.
heading: Limitations

text: The 302-run Planet Microbe arm measures presence or abundance without genes and supports only a negative biome contrast.
quote: **Marine arm is small and gene-blind** (302 PM runs; presence/abundance only), suitable only as a negative biome contrast.
